title: Paragraph structure
goal: Build a clear French paragraph: a topic sentence, an explanation, a concrete example and a closing sentence that links to what comes next.

items.fr: idée principale → explication → exemple → phrase de clôture
items.en: the four parts of a paragraph

drills.prompt: Which sentence works best as the topic sentence of a paragraph about public transit?
options: Le transport en commun présente plusieurs avantages pour les nouveaux arrivants.
Hier, j'ai pris le bus 55.
Par exemple, le métro passe toutes les cinq minutes.
drills.explain: A topic sentence announces the **one idea** the paragraph develops. The other two are details or examples.

drills.text: Le métro est rapide. ___, je vais de chez moi au bureau en vingt minutes.
drills.en: The metro is fast. For example, I get from my home to the office in twenty minutes.
drills.explain: The concrete case comes after [[Par exemple]] or [[Ainsi]], which proves the idea.

drills.text: ___ ce qui concerne le logement, les prix ont beaucoup augmenté.
drills.en: As far as housing is concerned, prices have gone up a lot.
drills.explain: [[En ce qui concerne…]] introduces the topic of a paragraph: *as far as… is concerned*.

example.fr: Chaque paragraphe développe une seule idée.
example.en: Each paragraph develops a single idea.

example.fr: L'idée principale est dans la première phrase.
example.en: The main idea is in the first sentence.

items.en: argument (a reason that supports an opinion)
items.note: Un argument is a supporting reason, not a quarrel. A quarrel is une dispute.

example.fr: Plusieurs villes, notamment Montréal et Gatineau, ont des pistes cyclables.
example.en: Several cities, in particular Montréal and Gatineau, have bike lanes.

items.en: thus, in this way (introduces an illustration or result)

example.fr: Ainsi, beaucoup de familles économisent de l'argent.
example.en: In this way, many families save money.

items.en: Let's take the example of Montréal.

items.fr: C'est le cas de ma voisine.
items.en: That's the case for my neighbour (a woman).
accept: C'est le cas pour ma voisine.

items.fr: En ce qui concerne le logement, …
items.en: As far as housing is concerned, …
accept: Pour ce qui est du logement, …

steps.title: Two versions of the same paragraph
steps.intro: Nguyen is writing a short text for his French class: *Peut-on vivre sans voiture à Montréal ?* Read his first draft, then the version his teacher helped him rewrite. Which one is easier to follow?

blocks.title: Version 1: the first draft
blocks.context: Everything is there, but in no particular order.
blocks.fr: Moi, j'habite sur le Plateau. Ma voisine a vendu sa voiture l'année passée. Le métro passe toutes les cinq minutes. L'hiver, c'est difficile de stationner. Il y a aussi BIXI. On peut vivre sans voiture à Montréal, je pense. Une voiture coûte cher.
blocks.en: I live on the Plateau. My neighbour sold her car last year. The metro comes every five minutes. In winter, it's hard to park. There's also BIXI. You can live without a car in Montréal, I think. A car is expensive.

blocks.title: Version 2: the rewritten paragraph
blocks.context: Same ideas, now in a clear order.
blocks.fr: À Montréal, il est tout à fait possible de vivre sans voiture, surtout si on habite près du centre. Tout d'abord, le réseau de transport en commun est dense : dans les quartiers centraux, le métro passe souvent toutes les cinq minutes aux heures de pointe, et plusieurs lignes d'autobus circulent jour et nuit. De plus, on peut utiliser BIXI, le service de vélos en libre-service, ou la voiture partagée quand on en a vraiment besoin. Prenons l'exemple de ma voisine : elle a vendu sa voiture l'année passée et elle économise maintenant plus de 600 $ par mois. Autrement dit, se passer de voiture, c'est non seulement pratique, mais aussi économique. Il faut cependant reconnaître que la situation est très différente en banlieue.
blocks.en: In Montréal, it is entirely possible to live without a car, especially if you live near downtown. First of all, the public transit network is dense: in the central neighbourhoods, the metro often comes every five minutes at rush hour, and several bus lines run day and night. What's more, you can use BIXI, the bike-share service, or car-sharing when you really need it. Let's take the example of my neighbour: she sold her car last year and now saves more than $600 a month. In other words, doing without a car is not only practical, but also economical. We must admit, however, that the situation is very different in the suburbs.

blocks.prompt: In Version 2, where is Nguyen's main idea?
options: In the first sentence
In the middle
Only in the last sentence
blocks.explain: A French paragraph usually **opens** with its main idea (the topic sentence). In Version 1, the opinion was hidden near the end, with [[je pense]].

blocks.prompt: What does the sentence about the neighbour do in Version 2?
options: It gives a concrete example that proves the idea
It introduces a new topic
It concludes the whole text
blocks.explain: [[Prenons l'exemple de…]] announces a real case. The number ([[600 $]]) makes it convincing.

blocks.prompt: Why does the last sentence mention the suburbs?
options: To add a limit and prepare the next paragraph
Because Nguyen lives in the suburbs
To repeat the main idea
blocks.explain: A good closing sentence can **open a door** to the next paragraph. Here, the next paragraph could discuss life without a car in the suburbs.

steps.title: How a French paragraph is built
steps.intro: In French writing, and especially in exams, a paragraph is not just a block of sentences. It is a small structured unit: **one paragraph = one idea**.

blocks.title: The four parts of a paragraph
head: Part
Its job
Useful openers
In Nguyen's paragraph
rows: State the one idea of the paragraph
En ce qui concerne… / Tout d'abord, … / Il est clair que…
À Montréal, il est tout à fait possible de vivre sans voiture.
Say why: give reasons and details
Tout d'abord, le réseau est dense… De plus, on peut utiliser BIXI…
Prove it with a concrete case: a person, a number, a place
Par exemple, … / Prenons l'exemple de… / C'est le cas de… / Ainsi, …
Sum up, or link to the next idea
Autrement dit, … / Bref, … / Il faut cependant reconnaître que…
Il faut cependant reconnaître que la situation est très différente en banlieue.
blocks.note: In an exam, aim for 4–6 sentences per paragraph. One sentence is not a paragraph; ten sentences usually mix several ideas.

blocks.title: Announcing the topic
blocks.pattern: En ce qui concerne + nom, …  /  Pour ce qui est de + nom, …
blocks.note: Both mean *as far as… is concerned*. Watch the contractions after **de**: [[pour ce qui est du logement]], [[de la santé]], [[des transports]]. In writing, you can also use [[Quant à…]] (*as for…*): [[Quant au logement…]]

examples.fr: En ce qui concerne le logement, les loyers ont beaucoup augmenté.
examples.en: As far as housing is concerned, rents have gone up a lot.

examples.fr: Pour ce qui est du climat, l'hiver est long mais ensoleillé.
examples.en: As for the climate, winter is long but sunny.

blocks.title: Giving a concrete example
blocks.pattern: Par exemple, …  /  Prenons l'exemple de + nom.  /  C'est le cas de + nom.  /  …, notamment + nom
blocks.note: [[notamment]] goes **inside** the sentence, just before the examples: *in particular*. [[Ainsi, …]] at the start of a sentence introduces an illustration or a result: *in this way*.

examples.fr: Prenons l'exemple de Toronto : le loyer moyen y dépasse 2 000 $.
examples.en: Let's take the example of Toronto: the average rent there is over $2,000.

examples.fr: Beaucoup de nouveaux arrivants, notamment les familles, cherchent un logement près d'une école.
examples.en: Many newcomers, in particular families, look for housing near a school.

examples.fr: C'est le cas de mon cousin, qui travaille à Moncton.
examples.en: That's the case for my cousin, who works in Moncton.

blocks.title: Words and phrases for this lesson
Common paragraph mistakes
blocks.body:
- **Starting with yourself:** [[Moi, je pense que…]] in the first line sounds like speech. In a written paragraph, start with the idea: [[Il est possible de vivre sans voiture à Montréal.]] You can give your opinion later, or say [[À mon avis, …]].
- **A list of facts, no links:** Version 1 is a list. Readers need connectors ([[tout d'abord]], [[de plus]], [[autrement dit]]) to see how the ideas fit together. You'll study many more in the next lesson.
- **Two ideas in one paragraph:** if you start with transport and end with the price of groceries, cut the paragraph in two.
- **Par exemple without an example:** [[Par exemple, c'est pratique.]] is not an example. An example is concrete: a person, a place, a number, a date.
- **Un argument is not a fight:** [[un argument]] is a reason that supports an opinion. A quarrel is [[une dispute]].

blocks.title: Why French teachers care so much about the plan
blocks.body:
French schools train students for years in the *plan*: introduction, développement, conclusion, with one idea per paragraph. Readers and examiners therefore **expect** to find the main idea at the start of each paragraph and a clear progression.

In the TEF and TCF writing tasks, part of the score is about **coherence and cohesion**: is the text organized, and are the ideas linked? A well-built paragraph with simple French often scores better than a messy one with fancy vocabulary.

blocks.title: Canadian details in Nguyen's text
blocks.body:
- **BIXI** is Montréal's bike-share system; Toronto has *Bike Share Toronto*. In French: [[le vélo en libre-service]].
- **La voiture partagée** or [[l'autopartage]] (car-sharing), for example *Communauto* in Québec.
- **La banlieue** = the suburbs. In Québec, people also say [[la Rive-Sud]] and [[la Rive-Nord]] for the suburbs around Montréal.
- In Québec, people say [[l'année passée]] and [[l'année dernière]] equally. Both are correct.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat the openers
blocks.note: When you read a paragraph aloud, pause briefly after each opener. The pause helps the listener follow your plan.

lines.fr: En ce qui concerne le logement, les loyers ont beaucoup augmenté.
lines.en: As far as housing is concerned, rents have gone up a lot.

lines.fr: Tout d'abord, le réseau de transport en commun est dense.
lines.en: First of all, the public transit network is dense.
lines.tip: tout d'abord: the t of tout is silent before d'abord.

lines.en: Let's take the example of my neighbour.
lines.tip: exemple: eg-zampl, with a z sound.

lines.fr: Plusieurs villes, notamment Montréal et Gatineau, ont des pistes cyclables.
lines.en: Several cities, in particular Montréal and Gatineau, have bike lanes.
lines.tip: notamment: no-ta-man, the final t is silent.

lines.fr: Autrement dit, c'est pratique et économique.
lines.en: In other words, it's practical and economical.

blocks.fr: Pour ce qui est de l'hiver, il ne faut pas en avoir peur. En effet, les villes canadiennes sont bien équipées : les trottoirs sont déneigés rapidement et les bâtiments sont bien chauffés. Prenons l'exemple de Québec : malgré la neige, les écoles ferment rarement.
blocks.en: As for winter, there's no need to be afraid of it. Indeed, Canadian cities are well equipped: sidewalks are cleared of snow quickly and buildings are well heated. Let's take the example of Québec City: despite the snow, schools rarely close.
blocks.prompt: What is the main idea of this paragraph?
options: You don't need to be afraid of winter in Canada.
Schools in Québec City often close.
Buildings in Canada are expensive to heat.
blocks.explain: The first sentence carries the idea: [[il ne faut pas en avoir peur]]. The rest explains ([[En effet]]) and gives an example ([[Prenons l'exemple de Québec]]).

blocks.fr: Beaucoup de nouveaux arrivants, notamment les familles, choisissent de s'installer en banlieue.
blocks.en: Many newcomers, in particular families, choose to settle in the suburbs.
blocks.prompt: Which word introduced a specific group?
options: notamment
autrement dit
pourtant
blocks.explain: [[notamment]] = *in particular*. It introduces a specific example inside the sentence.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Answer without scrolling back. Think about the **job** of each sentence.

blocks.prompt: Which is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about the cost of living in Vancouver?
options: À Vancouver, le coût de la vie est particulièrement élevé.
Par exemple, mon loyer est de 2 400 $.
Moi, j'aime beaucoup Vancouver.
Autrement dit, c'est cher.
optionFeedback: This is an example: it should come after the topic sentence.
This is a personal feeling, and it isn't about the cost of living.
Autrement dit sums up something already said: it can't start a paragraph.

blocks.prompt: Match each opener with its job in the paragraph.

blocks.text: Plusieurs provinces, ___ l'Ontario et le Nouveau-Brunswick, offrent des services en français.
blocks.en: Several provinces, in particular Ontario and New Brunswick, offer services in French.
blocks.explain: [[notamment]] goes inside the sentence, right before the specific examples.

blocks.prompt: Let's take the example of my neighbour (a man).

blocks.text: Pour ce qui est ___ logement, les prix ont beaucoup augmenté.
blocks.en: As for housing, prices have gone up a lot.
blocks.explain: de + le = [[du]]: [[pour ce qui est du logement]].

blocks.prompt: A paragraph is about public transit in Ottawa. Which sentence does **not** belong in it?
options: Les épiceries sont ouvertes le dimanche.
Le train léger relie l'est et l'ouest de la ville.
De plus, plusieurs lignes d'autobus circulent tard le soir.
Prenons l'exemple de mon trajet : je mets vingt minutes pour aller au travail.
blocks.explain: One paragraph = one idea. Grocery store hours are a different topic.

accept: En d'autres mots, c'est moins cher.
En d'autres termes, c'est moins cher.
Autrement dit, ça coûte moins cher.
blocks.explain: [[Autrement dit]] rephrases what you just said, often to sum it up. Note the comma after it.

blocks.prompt: That's the case for my sister.
accept: C'est le cas de ma sœur
blocks.explain: [[C'est le cas de…]] points to a real person who illustrates your idea.

blocks.text: C'est une ville ___ on peut vivre sans voiture.
blocks.en: It's a city where you can live without a car.
blocks.explain: Review (B1 unit 7): place → [[où]]. The relative pronoun lets you add details without starting a new sentence.

blocks.fr: Tout d'abord, le métro passe toutes les cinq minutes.
accept: Tout d'abord, le métro passe toutes les 5 minutes.
blocks.explain: [[tout d'abord]] = first of all; [[toutes les cinq minutes]] = every five minutes (feminine plural, with **toutes**).

blocks.prompt: Write one well-built paragraph on this question: “Is your city (or a city you know) a good place for newcomers?” Choose ONE aspect only: housing, transit, jobs, or services. Follow the four parts.
blocks.promptFr: Votre ville est-elle un bon endroit pour les nouveaux arrivants ? Écrivez un paragraphe sur un seul aspect.
checklist: A topic sentence with ONE idea, at the start
An explanation: tout d'abord / de plus…
A concrete example: Prenons l'exemple de… / C'est le cas de… (with a name, a place or a number)
notamment or ainsi at least once
A closing sentence: Autrement dit, … or a link to another aspect
4 to 6 sentences, no list of unrelated facts

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: En ce qui concerne les services, Gatineau est une ville très accueillante pour les nouveaux arrivants. Tout d'abord, plusieurs organismes offrent des cours de français gratuits et de l'aide pour chercher un emploi. De plus, la bibliothèque municipale organise des activités pour les familles, notamment des ateliers de conversation. Prenons l'exemple de mon amie Amira : elle est arrivée l'hiver passé et, grâce à ces services, elle a trouvé un emploi en trois mois. Autrement dit, on n'est jamais seul quand on s'installe à Gatineau. Il faut cependant reconnaître que le logement y est de plus en plus cher.
models.en: As far as services are concerned, Gatineau is a very welcoming city for newcomers. First of all, several organizations offer free French classes and help with finding a job. What's more, the municipal library organizes activities for families, in particular conversation workshops. Let's take the example of my friend Amira: she arrived last winter and, thanks to these services, she found a job in three months. In other words, you are never alone when you settle in Gatineau. We must admit, however, that housing there is more and more expensive.

summary:
- Build a paragraph in four parts: **topic sentence**, **explanation**, **concrete example**, **closing or transition**
- Announce a topic with [[En ce qui concerne…]] or [[Pour ce qui est de…]], and give examples with [[Prenons l'exemple de…]], [[C'est le cas de…]], [[notamment]] and [[ainsi]]
- Keep **one idea per paragraph** and sum up with [[Autrement dit, …]]

meta.notes: Fixed 'dans le Plateau' → 'sur le Plateau', removed the unverified VeloGO claim and lowered the Toronto rent figure to a safe one. Removed 'C'est-à-dire, …' from accepts and replaced the reorder distractor 'pour' (which formed an accepted variant) with 'à'.
